title: Longest Chunked Palindrome Decomposition
statement:
Cut the string `text` into `k` non-empty pieces `subtext_1, subtext_2, ..., subtext_k` which, placed back together in order, rebuild `text` exactly. The cut has to be mirror-symmetric at the level of pieces: for each `i` with `1 <= i <= k`, piece `subtext_i` must be the same string as piece `subtext_(k - i + 1)`. In other words the first piece matches the last one, the second matches the second-to-last, and so on (when `k` is odd, the middle piece is paired with itself).

Return the greatest `k` that such a cut can achieve.
constraints: text contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Look at the two ends of the string. If some prefix equals the suffix of the same length, peel off the **shortest** such pair: it never hurts. A longer matching pair `P`/`P` always contains the shorter match `Q` at both of its ends, so `P` can itself be split as `Q ... Q`, which only adds pieces. Repeating the greedy peel on the middle gives the maximum. When no prefix of the remaining middle equals its suffix, the whole middle has to be one piece.

The brute force tries every matching prefix length and recurses on the middle, which can branch exponentially.

## Approach

1. Keep the unmatched middle as `text[left .. right)`, start `count = 0` and try pieces of length `size = 1`.
2. While two pieces of length `size` fit in the middle, compare `front` (starting at `left`) with `back` (ending at `right`).
3. If they match, add 2 to `count`, move `left` forward and `right` back by `size`, and restart with `size = 1`.
4. Otherwise grow `size` by 1.
5. If characters remain in the middle (`left < right`), they form one extra piece.

## Example 1, step by step

`text = "ghiabcdefhelloadamhelloabcdefghi"` (length 32). With `left = 0`, `right = 32`: sizes 1 and 2 fail, size 3 matches `"ghi"`, so `count = 2`, `left = 3`, `right = 29`. Sizes 1 to 5 fail and size 6 matches `"abcdef"`: `count = 4`, `left = 9`, `right = 23`. Size 5 matches `"hello"`: `count = 6`, `left = 14`, `right = 18`. The middle `"adam"` has no match of size 1 or 2, and size 3 does not fit twice, so it becomes one piece: the answer is `7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²) in the worst case: comparing pieces of length 1 to s costs O(s²) before each peel of length s, and those lengths add up to at most n. A rolling hash makes each comparison O(1) for O(n) overall.
- Space: O(n) for the temporary substrings.

## Pitfalls

- Reset `size` to 1 after every match; a longer first match can skip pieces.
- The loop condition must leave room for two non-overlapping pieces: `2 * size <= right - left`.
- Add the middle piece only when it is non-empty; for `"aa"` the answer is 2, not 3.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | pieces peeled off both ends so far |
| `left`, `right` | the unmatched middle is `text[left .. right)` |
| `size` | length of the piece pair being tried |
| `front`, `back` | the candidate pieces at the start and end of the middle |
